mentl/ecb041a:
The stamp priced a second name field on LowFn and the interrogation
dissolved it. A nested fn binds its own name to its own handle, a
self-reference resolves through that bind, and the capture keeps the
handle it resolved to, while lower builds the closure with that same
handle. So "is this capture the closure being built" is one comparison of
two handles, needing no names at all.

self_capture_name replaces captures_self. Identity finds the capture, and
the read returns the name that capture reads, so the early bind targets
what the emitted body actually loads. The predecessor compared the
capture's name against the LowFn's name — two namespaces the moment the
nested-fn discriminator qualifies — and got the guard wrong and would have
bound the wrong local even had it fired. Both halves closed with fewer
fields, not more.

No byte-identity is claimed this time. The pin moved and the emit grew
seven lines against a smaller module because the source changed; m2 == m3
is the load-bearing reading, since it proves the new emit reproduces the
old one exactly on the wheel's own source. Nothing was being missed today,
so the fix is correct-for-the-future and neutral-for-the-present.

This is the third direction tried at this defect and the first that did
not have to be reverted. One name for the fn failed because the local
namespace is source-named; keeping the source name failed because the
symbol must qualify; carrying both was priced and then dissolved by
reading what the graph already connects.

What remains: the discriminator still reads a foreign slot through an open
row, so nothing qualifies yet and this fix is dormant. Re-attempting the
receiver annotation is the next step and the only known blocker left
between here and the row arc.

mentl/ec3e9b1:
`with field = config_arg` is a binding in the lexical scope of the handler's
config params. The state-init was lowered OUT of that scope (top-level pre-
registration), so `fold_handler(f, init) with acc = init` resolved `init` to a
non-existent global -> LUnresolved -> (unreachable). mentl2 trapped the moment
it ran fold during arm pre-registration (the real first-light blocker; the
effect-row-completeness theory was the wrong tail).

Fix, both layers, faithful to "handler IS state IS closure IS evidence": the
state inits lower in a frame with config names as captures (the same
pre_allocate_config_captures the arm bodies use), so a config reference becomes
LUpval(config_slot). emit reads it from the SAME record's config region (written
first) -- a state slot initialized from a config arg is one record reading
itself, not a re-derivation.

- src/lower.mn: lower_state_field_inits(config, state) wraps the lowering in a
  config-capture frame; HandlerDeclStmt pre-register passes config.
- src/backends/wasm.mn: emit_state_init_writes reads LUpval(slot) as
  (local.get $hstate)(i32.load offset=8+slot*4) of the record being built.
- seed: bootstrap/src/lower/walk_stmt.wat (config@20 from mk_handler_decl_full;
  reuses $pre_allocate_config_captures) + bootstrap/src/emit/emit_handler.wat
  (LUpval tag-305 record-relative read).

seed UNRESOLVED 29->27 (fold + take_collector); micros ev2/ev4/ev8=57, ev5=21,

mentl/eccec4d:
Morgan's catch: `~` is load-bearing in two of the five topological verbs
(`~>` handler-attach, `<~` feedback), so calling it "speculative inventory"
was imprecise — and the lexers were inconsistent. A standalone `?` already
lex-errored (no single-`?` token; `??` is the only `?` form), but a standalone
`~` lexed to TTilde and errored later at PARSE. Both characters exist ONLY
inside their two-char tokens, so the ultimate-consistent form treats them
identically:

- src/lexer.mn + bootstrap/src/lexer.wat: remove the standalone-`~` arm from
  single_char_kind. `~>`/`<~` are unaffected (maximal munch lexes them in
  two_char_kind before single-char is reached); a bare `~` now falls through
  to unexpected-char, exactly as `?` does.
- TTilde becomes a fully-dead enum slot. It would vanish like `::` did, but
  the seed's flat tag-space shares one counter with the Option ADT (deleting
  it cascade-renumbers None/Some) — pinned now, removed post-L1 with per-type
  tags. SYNTAX.md's TTilde note corrected to state all of this precisely.

Empirically regression-free: the wheel source has 100 `?` occurrences (in
comments and strings, including a "?" string literal) and `~>`/`<~`
everywhere; the census held at 165 exact (62/58/37/8) and the battery stayed
green (ev2/ev4/ev5/ev16, eq, interp), proving comments/strings are consumed
before punctuation classification and the verbs lex intact.
mentl/ec6f4fb:
Three landings that progress mentl2 from skeleton-only output to a structurally-valid m3 module:

(1) Hβ.first-light.handler-arm-ops-as-effect-ops — extend
$register_handler_decl_arm_ops to env_extend each arm op_name as
EffectOpScheme(handler_name) when not already bound. Wheel pattern:
`handler lower_scope { ls_push_scope() => ... }` IS the only
declaration of its arm ops; the handler_name doubles as the surface
effect-name. Each arm becomes Forall over fresh tyvars (param tyvars
per arg pattern + ret tyvar + row tyvar). Without this, perform sites
type as TError-hole and emit_lconst surfaces (unreachable), trapping
the wheel pipeline. Substrate parity with $infer_register_effect_ops.

(2) Hβ.first-light.unary-neg-stack-order — UNeg is `0 - x`, not
`x - 0`. Both seed ($ec6_emit_neg) and wheel (emit_unaryop) emitted
operand-then-zero-then-sub which computes x - 0 = x. The substrate
correct sequence: pop x to $state_tmp scratch, push 0, push x from
scratch, i32.sub. Same pattern as BConcat's state-threading at
emit_call.wat:309. Effect: ls_find_str_local now correctly returns
-1 for missing-key lookups; emit_start's `if ls_find_str_local(...,
"main", 0) >= 0` correctly takes the else branch when no main exists,
avoiding undefined-global-$main reference in m3.wat.

(3) Hβ.first-light.wheel-float-div-zero-guard — productive-under-
error per protocol_kernel_uniform_placeholder_substrate.md (chain-link
6 below cursor-is-the-substrate). Peer handle: #110
Hβ.emit.float-substrate-handler swaps the kernel-uniform i32 substrate
for typed f64 ops. Wheel parse_float trapped on i32.div_s 0 0 when
scanning float literals; zero-guard preserves L1 closure across the
wheel-side compile.

Result: mentl2 cleanly compiles wheel input through full pipeline;
wat2wasm-validates with --enable-tail-call (399KB); runs over wheel
input again producing valid 26-line m3.wat. Remaining gap is #111
(wheel-emit-implementation) — wheel's compile pipeline returns empty
